steps.text: This looks like an Atomic Red Team T1562.004 firewall rule manipulation test, so I'll score it as malicious and note the artifacts: host, process, command, the firewall rule registry entry, and the user identity, along with the fact that the rule gets deleted shortly after creation for cleanup verification.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, an interactive cmd.exe (proc-fe317db4a6) running as WORKSTATION5\wardog with High integrity launched netsh.exe (proc-154d2dd075) with the command 'advfirewall firewall add rule name="atomic testing" action=allow dir=in protocol=TCP localport=450'. The firewall service then wrote the matching allow rule to HKLM\...\FirewallPolicy\FirewallRules\{F7259D6F-...} (reg-0960adadbe, LPort=450, Dir=In). About 5 seconds later the same cmd.exe ran netsh again (proc-84b1d9017e) to delete the rule, and the registry key shows a matching delete. The rule name and the add-then-delete pattern match the Atomic Red Team test for T1562.004 (impair defenses by changing the firewall). That makes this a simulated attack rather than real administration. It is still defense evasion that opens an inbound port, so it is classed as malicious. Check that the rule is really gone and that the wardog account was used on purpose.
